description: Severity distribution for animal and insect contact — bites, stings, kicks, charging, envenomation. Covers domestic/farm animals, wildlife, insects, and marine creatures. Mostly non-SIF except for large animal crush/charge, venomous snake/spider, and anaphylaxis from stings. P(death) scale from AIS mortality data.
assumptions: Workplace context — agriculture, forestry, construction, utilities, veterinary
magnitude_note: Animal injury severity depends on the size/type of animal and whether envenomation or anaphylaxis is involved. Large animal injuries are mechanical (crush, kick — high kinetic energy), while insect/snake injuries are chemical/biological (venom, allergic response). Bands by hazard type.

magnitude_bands.description: Insect sting or minor bite without allergic response. Bee, wasp, ant, spider (non-venomous), tick, mosquito. Localised pain and swelling.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: CDC injury data: insect stings without anaphylaxis are self-limiting. ~60 sting deaths/year in US, almost all from anaphylaxis (separate band).
magnitude_bands.rationale: Without allergic response, insect stings cause localised pain and swelling only. P90=first_aid (antihistamine, ice). Not SIF. The risk is anaphylaxis in sensitised individuals (separate band).

magnitude_bands.description: Anaphylactic reaction to sting or bite in sensitised individual. Bee/wasp sting with known or unknown allergy. Systemic allergic response — airway swelling, cardiovascular collapse. Time-critical.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: CDC: ~60 insect sting deaths/year in US, virtually all anaphylaxis. With epinephrine within minutes, mortality <1%. Without treatment, anaphylaxis mortality ~5-10%.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Anaphylaxis without epinephrine auto-injector can be fatal within 30 minutes. P50=medical_treatment reflects hospital treatment for anaphylaxis. P90=serious_injury from severe reaction with delayed treatment. Adrenaline auto-injector is the critical mitigation (reduces P(death) by ~90%). Crosses SIF threshold at P90.

magnitude_bands.description: Venomous snake or spider bite. Relevant to agriculture, forestry, utilities, construction in endemic areas. Rattlesnake, brown snake, redback, funnel-web. Severity depends on species, venom load, and time to anti-venom.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: WHO snakebite data: ~100,000 deaths/year globally (mostly developing world). In developed countries with anti-venom access, mortality <1% for treated bites. Without treatment, some species (brown snake, taipan) have significant mortality.
magnitude_bands.rationale: In developed countries with hospital access, envenomation mortality is low (<1%). The unmitigated calibration (no anti-venom) gives P90=serious_injury from neurotoxic or haemotoxic effects. In remote locations without anti-venom or rapid evacuation, severity increases significantly — use the rescue_time modifier.

magnitude_bands.description: Dog bite or attack. Security dogs, stray dogs on construction sites, farm dogs. Also covers aggressive domestic animal bites (cat bites have high infection rate).
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: CDC: ~30-50 dog bite fatalities/year in US, mostly children. Adult workplace dog bites cause lacerations and puncture wounds. Fatal attacks on working-age adults are very rare.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Dog bites produce puncture wounds and lacerations. P90=medical_treatment for deep bite requiring sutures, antibiotics, possible tendon repair. Fatal dog attacks on working-age adults are exceptionally rare — most fatalities are children or elderly. Not SIF for adult workers.

magnitude_bands.description: Large animal kick, charge, crush, or trample. Horse, cattle, bull, pig. Farm/agricultural/equestrian setting. Large animals deliver enormous kinetic energy — a cow kick at 1 tonne is comparable to a low-speed vehicle strike.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: HSE agricultural fatality data: cattle and horses are leading causes of agricultural death in UK (~5-10 deaths/year from cattle alone). BLS: ~100 animal-related workplace deaths/year in US.
magnitude_bands.rationale: A cattle kick delivers ~500J — similar to a fall from 2m. A charging bull (500kg at 15km/h) delivers ~4kJ — comparable to a vehicle strike. P50=medical_treatment (fractures, crush injuries). P90=serious_injury from bull charge or being trampled/pinned against wall. Crosses SIF threshold at P90. Agricultural workers handling cattle are exposed to genuine SIF risk.

magnitude_bands.description: Large animal attack in confined space — cattle crush, horse stable, bull pen. Animal pins worker against wall or gate. No escape route. Combines large animal energy with entrapment.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: HSE agricultural fatality investigations: majority of cattle fatalities involve worker pinned in confined handling area. Bull in pen is one of the most dangerous routine agricultural scenarios.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Large animal in confined space = crush/pin mechanism. Worker cannot escape, animal repeats attack. A bull pinning a worker against a gate applies its full body weight (~800kg+). P50=serious_injury from crush fractures, organ damage. P90=fatality from sustained crush or head injury. This is the dominant agricultural SIF mechanism in the UK.

rescue_time.description: Multiplier on P(death). For envenomation and anaphylaxis, time to anti-venom/epinephrine is the primary survival factor. For large animal attacks, time to rescue from confined handling area. Agricultural and forestry settings are typically remote.

animal_size.description: Multiplier on P(death) for large animal bands. Scales with kinetic energy of charge/kick.

sources.author: HSE
sources.relevance: Agricultural fatality data — cattle and horses are leading causes. ~5-10 cattle-related deaths/year in UK. Majority involve worker pinned in confined handling area.

sources.author: CDC
sources.relevance: Insect sting deaths (~60/year, anaphylaxis), dog bite fatalities (~30-50/year), snakebite data.

sources.author: BLS
sources.relevance: Census of Fatal Occupational Injuries — ~100 animal-related workplace deaths/year in US.

sources.author: WHO
sources.relevance: Snakebite envenoming — global burden, anti-venom access, mortality data.

sources.author: Baker et al.
sources.relevance: AIS mortality rates — foundation for P(death) scale

validation_notes: STKY check: bull attack in pen should give P(SIF) > 0.50 — large_animal_confined P(SIF)=0.50 ✓
STKY check: bee sting (no allergy) should be NON_SIF — insect_sting_no_allergy P(SIF)=0.000 ✓
Cross-check: cattle handling is a genuine SIF risk — 5-10 UK deaths/year from a small exposed population. The per-event risk is comparable to working at height ✓

Key insight: large_animal_confined is the agricultural equivalent of caught_between — the animal is the 'moving object', the gate/wall is the 'fixed object'. The physics is the same as vehicle pinning.
